title: SignUpForm
wrapsNative: VStack of MonarchTextField with textContentType(.name) and (.username), MonarchPasswordInput with the .new purpose (the .newPassword content type), MonarchPasswordStrengthMeter, MonarchTermsAcceptance, MonarchButton and a Button with the Monarch link style; onSubmit
summary: A recipe, not a component: create an account with a name, an email and a new password, with the password rules, terms to accept, field errors and a link to sign in.
whenToUse: For the sign-up screen of an app that has its own accounts.
whenNotToUse: When the app creates accounts only through Rook ID, show MonarchSignInWithRookButton alone. To sign in, use the sign-in form recipe; to set up a workspace after sign-up, use the workspace onboarding recipe.
api: MonarchButton("Create account", variant: .primary, isLoading: isCreating, fullWidth: true, action: createAccount)

states.name: ready
states.description: Optional single sign-on above an "or" divider, the name, email and password fields, the strength meter with its rules, the terms checkbox, Create account and the sign-in line.

states.name: field errors
states.description: An empty name, an empty or malformed email, a password that misses a rule and unaccepted terms each show their error before anything is sent.

states.name: email taken
states.description: The server's answer goes on the email field; any other failure goes in a danger MonarchInlineNotice above the fields.

states.name: invitation
states.description: Prefill the email from an invitation and make it read-only by showing it as text instead of a field.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component in the theme: the title style heading, MonarchTextField and MonarchPasswordInput with their borders and errors, the strength meter's segments and rule list, the Monarch checkbox with document links, and a full-width primary button.
platformNotes: The web's SignUpForm is one component with onSubmit, its own messages and an optional confirm-password field. On iOS it is a recipe, because the request and navigation belong to the app. There is no confirm field: the password's reveal button shows typos, and the .newPassword content type that MonarchPasswordInput's new purpose sets lets iOS suggest a strong password and save it to the keychain with the app's associated domain. On a device add keyboardType(.emailAddress), textInputAutocapitalization(.never) and autocorrectionDisabled() to the email field (the sample page does); they are left out of the compiled example because the host build also targets macOS. Android composes the same recipe.
accessibility: The title has the header trait.
Field errors come from MonarchTextField and MonarchPasswordInput, which show and announce them in words.
The strength meter reads the strength and each rule as met or not met, so nothing depends on colour.
The terms checkbox is a standard toggle in the Monarch checkbox style; its required error is shown and read in words.
Create account and Sign in have 44-point touch targets.
edgeCases: Trim spaces around the name and the email but never change the password.
Validate on submit, not on every keystroke, so errors do not appear while the person is still typing.
Keep the rules the meter shows equal to the rules the server checks.
